design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (rate_lock_management)

1. Draw (draw_counts.py --task 0): {"prerequisite_problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 6, 6, 4]}. Assigned: relock 6, extension days 6, extension charge 6, builder-delay waiver 4.

2. Why a good test. The caller asks one thing: that Calloway's construction delay not cost him on his rate lock. The scored root is the builder-delay waiver amount on an extension charge, but at the opening there is no extension charge, no extension and the lock is expired. The agent must read from the waiver rule that it waits on an extension charge on the ledger, from the extension-charge rule that it waits on an extension recorded on the lock, and from the extension-days rule that an expired lock must first stand locked again (relocked). Each hop changes a number: the relock's relock_fee charge triggers the extension step-up, the extension's days and increments set the charge, the charge sets the waiver. Difficulty comes from reading policy, reconciling the lock ledger, the purchase agreement and ledger, the homesite reservation, warranty and insurance records, and from arithmetic; tools are one per problem with no near-synonyms.

3. Scope. Nothing occupied before (task 0). Claimed: lock_ext_builder_delay_relock, lock_ext_extension_days, lock_ext_extension_charge, lock_ext_builder_delay_waiver and tools relock_expired_lock_4b9eda82, extend_rate_lock_1be9088d (owner=user), assess_extension_charge_644b0045, waive_builder_delay_charge_21040a50. Reserved for task 1 (draw: 2 prerequisites, factors [6,6,5]): the request-stage tree — loan-amount resize to the loan-to-value limit, the buyer's upfront fee payment, and the lock confirmation (locked rate) — on disjoint subjects (lock_terms_changed, lock_fee_paid, lock_confirmed). No rate-sheet value exists in the schema, so float-down, worse-of relock, program change and new requests are not claimable; the builder-delay relock keeps the expired rate by declared overwrite.

4. Problem-tree card. Chain: lock_ext_builder_delay_relock -> lock_ext_extension_days -> lock_ext_extension_charge -> lock_ext_builder_delay_waiver (root).
 Edge A (extension_days <- relock): state_gate, gate rate_locks.status, form state. Sentence: "For a lock whose record carries an expired date, the extension days are worked out only once its status on record reads locked again and its relocks used count includes the relock that returned it to locked." Four-point test: connective "only once"; XX a record state (status, relocks used); no tool/id/code token; scope exactly the expired-lock case. Only the relock write moves an expired lock back to locked and counts a relock (the confirmation only moves requested->locked), so the reader resolves the hop to the relock. Opening: rate_locks.status = expired, relocks_used = 0. Deletion: status stays expired, downstream charge 1,179.82 and waiver 1,061.82, terminal charges_due 56.75 vs gold 1,566.92.
 Edge B (extension_charge <- extension_days): value_input, gate new_increments, form state, affirmative. Sentence: "The extension fee is fixed only after the lock record carries the extension it prices, its days counted in the extension days used beyond the extension days already charged on the lock ledger." Only the extension write raises extension days used. Opening: extension_days_used = 0. Deletion: charge recomputes to 0.
 Edge C (waiver <- extension_charge): value_input, gate charge_amount, form state, negated direction ("is not fixed until"), the way a waiver desk states it. Only the extension-charge write books extension_fee charges (the relock books relock_fee). Opening: ledger has only lock_fee_paid and lock_notice_sent. Deletion: no charge to act on, recompute raises.
 Directions: A "only once", B "only after", C "not ... until" — chosen per result. Order unique (single chain). Customer's own write: the extension (extend_rate_lock_1be9088d), handed over at its place; extending one's own lock is the buyer's decision over the lock he holds. No tool checks any prerequisite.

5. Base-invariant card. Relock: lock_expiry_relock.relock_window (time): anchor rate_locks.expired_date 2026-09-26 = day one, relock_window_days 30 (120-Day), last day 2026-10-25 accepted, 2026-10-26 refused; frozen 2026-10-13 = day 18. Extension: lock_extensions.extension_state (status locked) satisfied by prior step 10. Charge: lock_charge_assessed has no gate in lock_extensions, lock_expiry_relock, lock_float_down_option, lock_terms_change (policy_scope). Waiver: lock_builder_delay_waiver.one_waiver (dedup) — the named charge is new and uncollected. Overwrites declared: worse-of sentence (relock at expired rate when estimated completion stands later than contract completion), base relock-fee clause, base extension-fee clause, base waiver-percent clause; everything else inherited (max increments/days, relock window, never-waived relock charges).

6. Business-object card. Target: lock (120-Day Extended Lock) on purchase agreement MT-0418. The waiver acts on the latest extension_fee charge (booked at step 14) and names its charge number; the relock_fee charge from step 10 is excluded (relock charges are never waived). Upfront fee held 943.85 from receipts CHM-RCPT-41862 (500.00) and CHM-RCPT-41871 (443.85). Purchase ledger rows: deposits RCPT-HS-41907 (reservation transfer), RCPT-HP-42218, RCPT-HP-43561; closing date notices 2026-08-14 and 2026-09-22; buyer closing extension charge CHG-HP-4417 (the buyer's own week). The 2021 Larkspur Meadows agreement is closed and carries the active warranty.

7. Factor card (tier taken / baseline figure from the sensitivity run):
 Relock fee 1,510.17 (all-baseline 943.85): lapse day 18 -> +0.125 (1,132.62); relock LTV 90 (> 88) & score 712 -> +0.0625 (1,321.39); second_home -> +0.0625 (1,321.39); active warranty on another home -> -0.0625 (1,698.94); overhang 4 days -> +0.0625 (1,321.39); reminder 6 days before -> multiplier 0.5 + 6/20 = 0.8 (1,887.71). Near-misses (records the rule excludes): the lock row's stored ltv_pct 86.31 (a stored figure that is not the loan amount over the agreement's contract price and that no rule reads) would leave the add-on at zero, and the closed 2021 Larkspur Meadows agreement (contract price 489,990) would give 77%; the rule reads the lock's own agreement's contract price.
 Extension days 30 (baseline 15): Mesquite Trails +2; slip 56 -> 4; one buyer move +1; relocked & 17 days lapsed +2; notice 21 days +2; gap 10 +1; total 16 -> 2 increments. Removing any cushion gives 15.
 Extension charge 1,061.82 (baseline 943.86): step-up 1 + one relock_fee charge = 2 (707.88); 2 increments +0.03125 (750.00); both maxima +0.0625 (750.00); lead 30 -> -0.0625 (1,769.73); fee held -0.03125 (1,415.79); policy bound -0.03125 (1,415.79).
 Waiver 1,005.07 (baseline 1,061.82): builder share 56/63 (1,061.82); lapse rate 0.8 (1,061.82); late reminder +150 (855.07); fee paid in full within a day +100 (905.07). Near-miss: the buyer's own week (CHG-HP-4417) is excluded from the builder share.
 Cross-difficulty: purchase (several), homesite (occupancy), warranty (homeowner credit), insurance (binder credit). Multi-source: relock_ltv_score_add_on, lapse_cushion, extension_allowance_add_on, lapse_rate.

8. Persona. Nathaniel Osei, structural engineer, terse and slightly annoyed; opens with the goal and phone 7205550168; SSN 7342 when asked (DOB, ZIP as backup); passive answers about occupancy, the extra week, insurance, notices; agrees to fee-bearing steps after hearing the amount; runs the handed-over step with the given details; closes after the waiver amount. He never names expiry, relock, extension or charges.

9. Standard solution. find_customers(phone) -> verify(phone, ssn) -> read locks, lock ledger, purchase agreements, purchase ledger, homesite reservations, warranty, insurance -> relock (1,510.17, 6.5, 2026-11-12) -> buyer extends (30 days, 2 increments) -> charge 1,061.82 for 30 days -> waive 1,005.07 against the new charge number.

10. Verification. Handling-time recompute via check_compute's build_env/eval_compute on initial_state + prior gold writes (authoring scripts under /tmp, not shipped): P 1510.17, E1 30, E2 1061.82 (receipt LCK-CHG-4515), W 1005.07; per-factor baselines as listed. Skip runs give the edge effects in section 4. Gates are recorded in section 12.

11. Draft recomputation from visible context: the published waiver rule names its wait on an extension charge on the ledger; the charge rule waits on an extension recorded; the extension rule waits on an expired lock standing locked again; reading the locks finder (status expired) and the ledger (no charge) yields the same four writes in the same order and, with the factor rules, the same figures.

12. Revision: suite history maximum was 6 (< 8). The waiver's fourth factor now reads the lock ledger's fee payments (fee-standing goodwill) instead of the purchase deposit ledger, and the seeded upfront fee is two ach payments; figures unchanged (waiver 1,005.07). Per-task and suite gate outputs are recorded in worklog.md.

13. Round 2 (policy-task audit): F1 — base lock_extensions waiver sentence now named in the waiver's overwrite (lock_extensions added to base_policy_refs); F2 — the relock reminder multiplier now grows with the notice actually given (0.5 + lead/(2 x 10)), the slip cushion counts one day per 14 days of slip, the step-up multiplier is one plus the relock_fee charges counted, so each method tier computes a record-dependent quantity; F3 — every baseline paragraph states the default of each multiplier/share (starts at one); T0-4 — the relock LTV tier break moved to 88 and the stored ltv_pct (86.31, request-time figure against a price with options) now disagrees with the tier: a true near-miss; T0-6 — every half-up rounding adds 1e-7 before rounding so ties go up (1,887.705 -> 1,887.71); O1 — homeowner credit reads only a coverage on another agreement; O2/O3 — docstrings carry no ordering word and no hint of a separate charge; O4 — all seven tool suffixes redrawn, one uuid4 call each; O5 — 'that relock' reworded. Charges due at the end: 1,566.92.

14. Round 3 (revision_2): N1/T0-7 — the sentence 'Calloway bears only the part of an extension charge that the builder delay caused ...' is removed from the waiver rule; the formula sentence (share x lapse rate plus the two goodwill terms, capped at the charge) is the only amount sentence, so one waiver amount remains. T0-O6 — the stale ltv_pct is described only as a stored figure that disagrees with the record-derived ratio (no unsupported origin claimed). O10 — missing_reminder_mult lowered to 0.4 so the 'no reminder' tier never coincides with the late tier's floor. O11 — the relocked step-up also adds prior_increment_step per earlier increment, so that tier varies with the record. O4-r2 — confirmation tool suffix redrawn. Task 0 scored values unchanged.
user_scenario:
You are Nathaniel Osei, a 47-year-old structural engineer who lives in Castle Rock, Colorado, and is buying a winter home from Calloway Homes in Mesquite Trails in Buckeye, Arizona: lot MT-0418, The Saguaro, Elevation B. You are financing it through Calloway Home Mortgage. You speak in short, precise sentences, you are polite but you do not hide that you are annoyed, and you like to hear the reason behind a number before you accept it.

You call because Calloway's construction is behind. The house was supposed to close in late September; Calloway's construction team pushed the closing to November because the home is not finished, and you are now set to close on November 16. What you want from this call is simple: you do not want Calloway's construction delay to cost you anything on your mortgage rate lock with Calloway Home Mortgage, and you want the agent to take care of whatever the lock needs today. You open by saying roughly that, and you give the phone number on your profile, 7205550168, so they can find you. You do not know how lock pricing works and you never suggest what should be done; you leave that to the agent.

When the agent asks you to confirm your identity, you give the last four of your Social Security number, 7342. If they ask for something else, your date of birth is August 22, 1979 and your mailing ZIP code is 80104. You never recite everything at once; you answer what you are asked.

If the agent asks about the home itself, it is a second home that you and your wife plan to spend winters in; your main home is the Calloway house you bought in Larkspur Meadows in 2021, and you still own it. If the agent asks why the closing moved a further week, you explain that after Calloway's new date came out you asked to push closing back one week so you could fly down for it. If the agent asks about homeowners insurance, Calloway Insurance Agency sent you a binder at the beginning of October. If the agent asks when you were told about the delay, you remember a closing date notice from Calloway in the third week of September and an email reminder about your rate lock around September 19, about a week before the end of that month, which you did not act on because you assumed Calloway would sort it out.

If the agent explains that something has to be done on the lock and that it carries a fee you will owe, you say you do not love it, ask them to tell you the amount, and then agree to let them go ahead, because you would rather keep your rate. If the agent tells you that a step on the lock is one you have to take yourself and hands it to you, you carry it out right away with exactly the details the agent gives you, and then you tell the agent what the confirmation said. Whenever the agent quotes a figure, you ask once how it was arrived at, and you accept the explanation.

Once the agent tells you that the part of the cost caused by Calloway's delay has been taken off and tells you the amount, you ask whether that is the final word; if the agent says it is, you thank them and end the call. If what is taken off is less than the whole charge, you say you had hoped it would be all of it, but if that is how it is figured you accept it. You do not ask for anything else.

Relock fee percent = relock_fee_pct 0.25 (120-Day Extended Lock) + lapse add-on 0.125 (lapse day 18 counted from expired date 2026-09-26 to 2026-10-13, at or after lapse_late_from_day 15) + loan-to-value and score add-on 0.0625 (relock loan-to-value 377,541.00 / 419,490.00 = 90% above 88, score 712 below 720; the stored ltv_pct 86.31 is not the rule's quotient) + occupancy add-on 0.0625 (converted reservation occupancy second_home) - homeowner credit 0.0625 (active HomeCare 1-3-10 Plus coverage on the Larkspur Meadows home, another agreement) + closing-reach add-on 0.0625 (scheduled closing 2026-11-16 is 4 days after 2026-10-13 + 30) = 0.5; 377,541.00 x 0.5% = 1,887.705 -> 1,887.71 (half up), above the 350.00 floor; expiry reminder multiplier = late_reminder_floor_mult 0.5 + reminder lead 6 / (2 x 10) = 0.8 because the reminder of 2026-09-19 came 6 days before the 2026-09-25 expiration (fewer than 10): 1,887.71 x 0.8 = 1,510.168 -> 1,510.17.
